The page gives no states for April 1864 (the infobox map caption lists none), only 'the port of Veracruz, the capital Mexico City, and other major cities as north as Monterrey and as south as Oaxaca'; the shape is the Mexican Monarchists row's 1864 territory (another dossier) plus Monterrey. keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 2.006 M km2, the whole of Mexico (the modern country is 1.96 M km2): the Empire's claim, which the pages do not support as control. The infobox gives no area to compare. The Empire 'was divided into 50 departments' by the law of 13 March 1865 but 'not all could be administered during the war'; Juárez's government moved 'north toward the border' and the French entered Chihuahua City, 'the provisional capital of the Republic', on 15 August 1865 (Second French intervention page). The corrected shape is the land the pages show imperialist-held; the Federated Republic dossier keeps the same land as Republican soil under hatched occupation.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1867: Cliopatria's 1866-1867 shape still covers all Mexico, but by 1867 the Republicans held the country outside a few cities. Bazaine 'evacuated Mexico City on 5 February 1867', Veracruz was left to the imperialist General Pérez Gómez, Maximilian reached Querétaro on 19 February and the siege began on 5 March; Chihuahua fell in March. Only the cities the pages name are drawn; a gap-filler should open the Querétaro campaign for the rest (Puebla, Guanajuato's Mejía garrison).

The date and the capital are the page's; the territory is the Mexican Monarchists row's, because the page lists no states.

ledger.note: 15 August 1865: the French enter Chihuahua City. 'He entered Chihuahua City, the provisional capital of the Republic, on 15 August'; Juárez fled to the border.
1866: the Republicans retake Tampico. 'The Republican Aureliano Rivera captured Tampico in May'; the French surrendered it in July and Tuxpan in August.

region.text: 'other major cities as north as Monterrey'

ledger.note: 25 July 1866: the Imperialists evacuate Monterrey. 'Monterrey was evacuated by the Imperialists on 25 July'.
4 August 1866: Saltillo is evacuated. 'Saltillo on 4 August'; the French withdrawal had let the Republicans into Parras in June.
September 1866: the French leave Guaymas, in Sonora ('The French withdrew in September'); the page also has the Republican Ángel Martínez briefly in Hermosillo on 4 May.

region.text: Oaxaca, taken by the imperialists in early 1865

ledger.note: 1 November 1866: Oaxaca City falls to Díaz. 'Oaxaca City fell on 1 November'.
November 1866: Matamoros falls to the Republicans. 'In November, Matamoros fell to the Republicans with the aid of U.S. troops.'
13 November 1866: the French complete the evacuation of Mazatlán, in Sinaloa.
November 1866: Durango is evacuated by the French ('French troops evacuated it in November'); the page does not say who held it.

December 1866: Guadalajara is abandoned. 'Guadalajara was abandoned by the French on 12 December 1866', and the imperialists evacuated the city on 19 December; on 19 December Napoleon III announced that all French troops would be withdrawn.

region.text: Chihuahua City, 'the provisional capital of the Republic', entered on 15 August 1865

ledger.note: March 1867: Chihuahua City falls to the Republicans. 'Billot left the city on 31 January, and it fell to Republican troops in March.'

15 May 1867: Querétaro falls. The city 'held out until being betrayed by an imperial officer who opened the gates to the liberals on 15 May 1867'; Maximilian was captured there (the Second French intervention page puts the opening of the gates on the night of 14 May).

wars.outcome: Republican victory: the French withdrew (Napoleon III announced it on 19 December 1866; Bazaine left Mexico City on 5 February 1867 and the last troops sailed on 12 March), Querétaro fell on 15 May 1867 and Maximilian was executed on 19 June 1867.
wars.note: Dates before 1865 (the intervention began 8 December 1861 at Veracruz) are on the page but are not this dossier's years.

certainty.note: The Empire claimed all Mexico but held cities and corridors; no treaty line is dated on the pages, and the frontier with the United States is the Rio Grande only as a river (the page names none). All soft.

notes: Cliopatria's single row is the Empire as a claim over the whole country (2.0 M km2, 1865-1867); the pages show a regime holding the centre and some cities. The Federated Republic dossier (am-08-c) reads the same land as Republican soil under hatched Imperial occupation; this dossier mirrors those occupation events with the roles reversed and carries its own corrected extent (1864 core + Monterrey; 1865 adds Oaxaca and Chihuahua; 1867 only Mexico City, Querétaro, Veracruz). The renderer must not draw the 1865-1867 Cliopatria shape on top of the Federated Republic's land. Mexican Monarchists (1864) is the Regency, the same regime; its dossier ends in April 1864 and 1864 is drawn by both. Budget 2 pages: the Querétaro campaign, Puebla, Guanajuato (Mejía's garrison), Yucatan and the 1865 departments were not opened; the 50 departments of the law of 13 March 1865 cannot be mapped. The Empire as a French client state (vassalage to the Second French Empire) is not recorded because neither page states it in a sentence with a date. Gazetteer: all names resolve. Page budget used: 2 of 2.
